## Exam 48 — Part 3: Building Renovation Noise

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a tenant and a building manager about construction noise.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN:	Hello, I'm calling about the construction noise in the building. It's been extremely loud for the past week, and I'm finding it impossible to work from home. I'm in apartment 304.

MAN:	I understand your concern, Ms...?

WOMAN:	Johnson. Sarah Johnson.

MAN:	Thank you, Ms. Johnson. I apologize for the inconvenience. We're currently renovating the lobby and hallways on the first three floors. The work is scheduled to continue for another two weeks, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

WOMAN:	Two more weeks? That's going to be a serious problem for me. I have several important video meetings with clients, and the drilling and hammering make it impossible to conduct them professionally. Is there any way to reduce the noise levels, especially during business hours?

MAN:	I completely understand your situation. While we can't stop the construction entirely, we might be able to adjust the schedule for the noisiest work. Would it help if we limited the heavy drilling to between 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m.? That way, you could plan your meetings around those times.

WOMAN:	That would be somewhat better, but I often have meetings throughout the day. Is there any other accommodation you could offer? Perhaps a temporary reduction in rent or access to a quiet space in the building where I could work?

MAN:	Actually, we do have a small conference room on the fifth floor that isn't being used much these days. It's quiet up there since the construction hasn't reached those floors yet. I could arrange for you to have access to it during business hours for the duration of the construction period.

WOMAN:	That sounds like it could work. Is there Wi-Fi available in that room? And would I need to reserve it, or could I just use it whenever I need to?

MAN:	Yes, there's Wi-Fi throughout the building, including the conference room. You wouldn't need to reserve it formally, but I'd suggest checking with the front desk before heading up, just to make sure no one else is using it. I can add your name to the approved list right away.

WOMAN:	That's very helpful, thank you. And about the drilling schedule change you mentioned - would that start tomorrow?

MAN:	Absolutely. I'll speak with the construction supervisor this afternoon to ensure the heavy work is limited to the 12:00 to 2:00 p.m. timeframe starting tomorrow. And I'll email you the access code for the conference room within the hour.

WOMAN:	Perfect. I appreciate your help with this. It's a relief to know I'll have options for the next couple of weeks.

## Exam 48 — Part 5: Shopping Mall Upgrades

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions

### Audio Transcript
A:	Thanks for coming in today. As you know, we need to finalize our renovation plans for the mall. The board wants our recommendations by next week.
B:	Right. The mall's definitely showing its age. Those beige tiles from the 90s have got to go.
C:	Absolutely. And the lighting is terrible – so dim in some areas. I've had several store owners complain that customers can't even see their merchandise properly.
A:	So we have a few options to consider. The first proposal focuses on updating the food court and adding more seating. The second is more about modernizing the main walkways and entrances.
B:	I'm leaning toward the second option. First impressions matter, and those entrances look dated. Plus, widening the walkways would make the whole place feel more spacious.
C:	Mmm, I see your point, but the food court is where people gather. If we make that area more attractive with better seating and maybe some charging stations, people might stay longer and shop more.
A:	Both good points. What about budget concerns? The walkway renovation is about 15% more expensive.
B:	True, but it affects the entire shopping experience. The food court is just one section of the mall.
C:	Well, what if we did a hybrid approach? Focus on the main entrance – that's what everyone sees first – and then do a scaled-down renovation of the food court?
A:	That could work. We'd have to trim some elements from both plans though.
B:	I'm not so sure about that. Doing half measures might end up looking inconsistent. You know what I mean? Like the mall can't decide what it wants to be.
C:	Fair enough. But we could phase it – do the entrances this year and budget for the food court next year?
A:	That's actually not a bad idea. The board might go for that approach.
B:	And what about the store facades? Some of them look like they haven't been updated since the mall opened.
C:	We could include guidelines for store renovations as part of our plan. Maybe even offer some incentives for stores that update within the next year.
A:	I like that. So it sounds like we're leaning toward the entrance and walkway renovations first, with a phased approach for the food court, and some guidelines for store owners.
B:	Yeah, that makes sense to me.
C:	Same here. Should we meet again on Friday to finalize the details before presenting to the board?
A:	Perfect. I'll draft something up and send it around before then.

## Exam 49 — Part 1: Community Centre Membership

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman at a neighborhood welcome event. The woman is a community center coordinator, and the man is a new resident in the area.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Good morning! Welcome to our neighborhood welcome event. I haven't seen you at our community gatherings before. Are you new to the area?
MAN: Yes, I just moved here last week from Edmonton. I'm still trying to get my bearings around the neighborhood. There seems to be a lot going on here.
WOMAN: Absolutely! That's why we host these welcome events. I'm Sarah, by the way. I coordinate activities at the community center.
MAN: Nice to meet you, Sarah. I'm Michael. I was hoping to find out about recreational facilities in the area. I used to play basketball regularly in Edmonton, and I'd like to continue that here.
WOMAN: You're in luck! Our community center has a full-size basketball court that's open Monday through Friday from 4 to 9 p.m., and weekends from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.
MAN: That sounds perfect. Is there a membership fee or something I need to sign up for?
WOMAN: Yes, you'll need a community center membership. It's $120 for the year or $15 monthly. The annual membership gives you access to all our facilities, including the gym and swimming pool.

MAN: I think I'll go with the annual membership. It seems like a better deal in the long run. Do you have any basketball leagues or pickup games that I could join?
WOMAN: We actually have a recreational league that plays every Tuesday and Thursday evening. They're always looking for new players. And there's usually pickup games on Saturday mornings around 11.
MAN: That's exactly what I was hoping for! Um, is there a separate registration for the league, or is that covered by the membership?
WOMAN: The league has a small additional fee of $50 per season to cover referee costs and equipment. The next season starts in two weeks, so your timing is perfect.
MAN: Great! And what about the registration process? Can I sign up today?
WOMAN: Absolutely. I can help you with the paperwork right now. We'll need some basic information and a photo ID for your membership card. Oh, and there's a special promotion this month – new members get a free fitness assessment with one of our trainers.
MAN: That sounds like a great deal. I've been meaning to get back into shape after the move.

WOMAN: Here's your membership card, Michael. You're all set! The fitness assessment can be scheduled at the front desk whenever you're ready.
MAN: Thanks so much, Sarah. Actually, I was wondering about other activities at the center. My daughter is coming to live with me next month, and I'd like to find something for her too. She's 12 and really into arts and crafts.
WOMAN: We have several youth programs that might interest her. There's a weekly art class on Wednesday afternoons, and a crafting club that meets on Saturdays. Both are included in your family membership.
MAN: Oh, I didn't realize I could get a family membership. How much extra would that be?
WOMAN: It's only $60 more for the year, so $180 total. That covers all immediate family members living in your household. You can upgrade today if you'd like.

## Exam 49 — Part 3: Riverside Garden Plot Signup

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions

WOMAN:	Hi there! I just moved to the neighborhood and I'm interested in getting a garden plot this season. I've always wanted to grow my own vegetables, and I noticed your garden while walking around last weekend.
MAN:	We'd be happy to have you join us! We do have a few plots available for this growing season. The standard plot size is 10 by 12 feet, and the annual fee is $75, which includes water access and use of our communal tools.
WOMAN:	That sounds reasonable. What kinds of things do people typically grow here? I'm thinking about tomatoes, peppers, and maybe some herbs, but I'm not sure what grows well in this climate.
MAN:	All of those grow wonderfully here! Most members grow a mix of vegetables and flowers. Tomatoes, zucchini, and leafy greens are very popular. We also have a community herb garden that everyone can use, so you might want to save your space for other plants.
WOMAN:	Oh, that's good to know about the herb garden. Are there any rules I should be aware of before I sign up?
MAN:	Yes, we do have a few guidelines. We're an organic garden, so no chemical pesticides or fertilizers are allowed. Members are also expected to maintain their plots regularly and participate in at least two community workdays per season, which are usually on Saturday mornings.
WOMAN:	That makes sense. I work weekdays, so Saturday workdays would be perfect for me. How soon could I start planting if I register today?
MAN:	You could start as early as this weekend! The soil has already been tilled, and many members have begun planting cool-weather crops. If you'd like to register, I'll need you to fill out this form and pay the annual fee. We accept cash, check, or e-transfer.
WOMAN:	Great! I'll fill out the form now. Do you offer any resources for beginners? This will be my first garden, and I'm a bit nervous about killing everything.
MAN:	Absolutely! We have monthly workshops for beginners, and our next one is this Sunday at 2 PM on spring planting techniques. Plus, many of our experienced gardeners are happy to offer advice. We also have a small library of gardening books you can borrow.
WOMAN:	That's perfect. I'll definitely come to the workshop on Sunday. I'm really looking forward to meeting other gardeners and learning from them.
MAN:	Wonderful! Once you've completed the registration, I'll assign you plot number 17, which gets good sun exposure and is near the water spigot. I'll also email you our welcome packet with the garden map and calendar of events.

## Exam 49 — Part 5: Garden Expansion Layout

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three community garden members. They are meeting to discuss plans for expanding their neighborhood garden.

### Audio Transcript
A:	Thanks for meeting today, everyone. As you know, the city has approved our request to expand the community garden into that vacant lot next door. We need to figure out how to best use this new space.
B:	This is such great news! I've been on the waitlist for a plot for almost a year now. How much extra space are we talking about?
A:	It's about 4,000 square feet, which could give us room for maybe 15 to 20 new garden plots, depending on how we divide it up.
C:	That sounds promising, but I'm wondering if we should use all the space just for individual plots. What about creating some communal areas? Maybe a shared herb garden or a small orchard?
B:	Oh, I like that idea. We could even set aside a section for native plants to attract pollinators. That would benefit everyone's gardens.
A:	Mmm, those are good suggestions. We'd need to figure out who would maintain the communal spaces though. Our individual plots work well because everyone's responsible for their own area.
C:	We could set up a rotation system. Each member takes a turn caring for the communal spaces, maybe once a month or so.
B:	That could work. I'd be happy to pitch in. What about water access? The current garden only has two spigots, and they're already pretty busy on hot days.
A:	You're right about that. I've actually talked to the city about installing two more water sources in the new section. They seemed open to it, but we'd need to cover part of the cost.
C:	How much are we talking about?
A:	Roughly $800 for both, which isn't set in stone yet. We have about $1,200 in our community garden fund right now.
B:	Well, that would leave us with $400 for other expenses. What about tools? We'll need more with all these new gardeners joining us.
C:	I'm not so sure about buying more tools. Our shed is already packed to the gills. Maybe we could ask new members to bring their own basic tools?
A:	That's a fair point. We could require the basics like trowels and pruners, but still provide the larger shared items like wheelbarrows and shovels.
B:	Sounds reasonable. When do you think we can start preparing the new space?
A:	The city says we can begin next month. I was thinking we could organize a community workday to clear the area and mark out the new plots.
C:	Great idea. I can create a sign-up sheet and post it on our bulletin board. Should we meet again next week to finalize the layout?
A:	Perfect. I'll bring some draft designs, and we can go from there.

- 3. To help with pollination for all gardens
- 4. To create a visually attractive entrance
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To satisfy city requirements: No city requirements about native plants are mentioned.
❌ 2. To reduce maintenance needs: Maintenance reduction isn't mentioned as a benefit of native plants.
✅ 3. To help with pollination for all gardens: Person B specifically suggests "a section for native plants to attract pollinators. That would benefit everyone's gardens."
❌ 4. To create a visually attractive entrance: Aesthetics aren't mentioned as a reason for native plants.

## Exam 49 — Part 6: Transit Expansion Funding

You will hear a presentation about public transit expansion in Canadian cities.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** Which two Canadian cities are specifically mentioned as having recent transit expansion projects?

- 3. Ottawa and Edmonton
- 4. Burnaby and Toronto
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Montreal and Calgary: While both cities are mentioned, they aren't identified as having recent transit expansion projects.
✅ 2. Toronto and Vancouver: The content specifically states "Toronto's recent completion of the Eglinton Crosstown LRT and Vancouver's Broadway SkyTrain extension are prime examples" of transit expansion.
❌ 3. Ottawa and Edmonton: These cities aren't mentioned in the content at all.
❌ 4. Burnaby and Toronto: While Burnaby is mentioned as an area affected by transit expansion near Vancouver, it isn't identified as having its own transit expansion project.

**Q2:** According to the Canadian Urban Transit Association, why is investing in public transit economically beneficial?
- 1. Because it creates more construction jobs in urban areas
- 2. Because it increases tourism revenue in downtown areas
- 3. Because it reduces congestion, lowers emissions, and increases property values
- 4. Because it allows for more efficient delivery of goods and services
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Because it creates more construction jobs in urban areas: The content doesn't mention job creation as an economic benefit.
❌ 2. Because it increases tourism revenue in downtown areas: Tourism revenue is not mentioned in the content.
✅ 3. Because it reduces congestion, lowers emissions, and increases property values: The content directly states "According to a recent study by the Canadian Urban Transit Association, every dollar invested in public transit generates approximately $4 in economic returns through reduced congestion, lower emissions, and increased property values."

**Q3:** How do Dr. Wilson and Sarah Patel differ in their views on transit expansion?

- 4. Wilson opposes gentrification while Patel supports community displacement

- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. Wilson believes it's essential for sustainable growth while Patel questions if the costs are justified: The content states that Dr. Wilson "argues that investing in public transportation is essential for sustainable city growth" while Sarah Patel "question[s] whether the massive costs are justified."

❌ 4. Wilson opposes gentrification while Patel supports community displacement: Neither of these positions is attributed to Wilson or Patel in the content.

**Q4:** What concern does Michael Thompson raise about transit expansion?

- 2. It reduces parking availability in residential areas
- 3. It leads to higher housing prices that displace original residents

❌ 2. It reduces parking availability in residential areas: This concern isn't mentioned in the content.
✅ 3. It leads to higher housing prices that displace original residents: The content states "Community advocate Michael Thompson notes that while transit access improves, many original residents can no longer afford to live in these upgraded neighborhoods."

❌ 4. She favors bus systems exclusively over rail transportation: The content doesn't mention Rahman's preference for any specific transit mode.

**Q6:** What environmental benefit of public transit is mentioned in the presentation?

- 2. It reduces the need for parking lots downtown

## Exam 5 — Part 1: Beginner Photography Workshop

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman at a photography studio. The woman teaches at the studio, and the man has just come in.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi, um, sorry to bother you. I saw your poster about a photography course for beginners?
WOMAN: No bother. I teach that course, actually. Are you just starting out?
MAN: Very much so. I bought my first real camera last week, just a basic digital one. The guy at the store pushed a twelve-hundred-dollar model, but I want to see if I stick with it first.
WOMAN: Honestly? Smart move. Half my students show up with expensive gear they're scared to touch. Can you set yours to manual?
MAN: I think so, there's a dial with an M on it. But I leave it on automatic, and my shots of the herons at the marsh near my place all come out blurry.
WOMAN: That's really common. Birds move fast. Our Camera Basics course would sort that out. Six weekly classes, two hours each, and the last one's an outdoor shoot.
MAN: That's what I need. What does it cost?
WOMAN: Two hundred and sixty for the course, plus a forty-five-dollar materials fee. That covers your workbook.
MAN: Okay. And when are the classes?
WOMAN: There are two groups. Saturday mornings from ten to noon, or Tuesday evenings from seven to nine. Both start the week after next.
MAN: Saturdays would be ideal. My weeknights are kind of a mess.
WOMAN: Let me check how many Saturday spots are left.

WOMAN: Oh, shoot. I'm sorry, my Saturday group's full. Someone took the last spot yesterday afternoon.
MAN: Oh. Well, that's a letdown. Is there a waiting list, at least?
WOMAN: There is, but four people are already on it, and hardly anyone drops out once they've paid. The next Saturday course starts in January. I'll be taking names for that one in December, if you like.
MAN: January? I was hoping to get some decent heron shots before they fly south for the winter. What about Tuesdays?
WOMAN: Tuesdays still have lots of room. There are only five people signed up so far.
MAN: Ugh. Tuesday's my hockey night. Well, every second Tuesday, anyway. Our rec league plays at eight, and I'm the only goalie on my team.
WOMAN: Hmm. So you'd be missing three of the six classes. That's a lot for a beginner course.
MAN: Yeah, I know. I was really looking forward to this, too. I even bought a camera bag yesterday.
WOMAN: Don't give up just yet. Arjun teaches the Tuesday group, and he's in the back right now. Let me go and ask him something.
MAN: Sure, go ahead. I'm not going anywhere.

WOMAN: Okay, good news, I think. Arjun records every Tuesday class, so on your hockey weeks, you could watch it online the next day.
MAN: Hmm. A video's not really the same as someone showing you on your own camera, though.
WOMAN: That's the other part. Arjun runs a catch-up session on Saturday afternoons, from one to half past two, for anyone who missed that week. It's usually just three or four people, so it's very hands-on.
MAN: Oh, that's not bad. Could I just book private lessons on those weeks instead?
WOMAN: You could, but they're ninety dollars an hour. The catch-up is included in the course. When's your first hockey Tuesday?
MAN: The fourteenth, I think.
WOMAN: Then your first catch-up would be Saturday the eighteenth.
MAN: Okay. I'd still be paying full price, though, and I'd only be in class half the time.
WOMAN: That's fair. I can't change the course fee, that's up to the owner. But I can take off the forty-five-dollar materials fee. You'd still get the workbook.
MAN: Seriously? Okay, you've talked me into it.
WOMAN: Great! Let me grab you a form. Oh, and bring your camera's manual to the first class. Most people never open theirs.
MAN: Ha. Mine's still in the box, in the plastic.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the man trying to do?
- 1. Exchange the camera he bought last week
- 2. Join a class that teaches camera skills
- 3. Get advice on buying a more expensive camera
- 4. Have his new camera checked for a problem
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Exchange the camera he bought last week: He says he 'bought my first real camera last week', but he never asks to return or swap it; he has come about the 'photography course for beginners'.
✅ 2. Join a class that teaches camera skills: He opens with 'I saw your poster about a photography course for beginners?' and, after hearing the times, says 'Saturdays would be ideal.'
❌ 3. Get advice on buying a more expensive camera: The store 'pushed a twelve-hundred-dollar model', but he chose 'just a basic digital one' and never asks about buying a better camera.
❌ 4. Have his new camera checked for a problem: His shots 'come out blurry' because 'I leave it on automatic', and the woman says 'That's really common', so nothing is wrong with the camera.

**Q2:** How does the woman feel about the camera the man chose?
- 1. She wishes he had bought the pricier model
- 2. She thinks he spent too much money on it
- 3. She believes a simple one was a wise start
- 4. She is surprised that it takes blurry photos
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She wishes he had bought the pricier model: The pricier model is the 'twelve-hundred-dollar model' he turned down, and she calls his choice a 'Smart move.'
❌ 2. She thinks he spent too much money on it: He bought 'just a basic digital one'; the expensive gear she mentions belongs to other people ('Half my students show up with expensive gear').
✅ 3. She believes a simple one was a wise start: When he says he wants 'to see if I stick with it first', she answers 'Honestly? Smart move.'
❌ 4. She is surprised that it takes blurry photos: She is not surprised by the blurry shots. She says 'That's really common. Birds move fast.'

**Q3:** When does another Saturday course start?
- 1. In December
- 2. In two weeks
- 3. In the spring
- 4. In January
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. In December: December is only when she will be 'taking names for that one', not when the course begins.
❌ 2. In two weeks: Two weeks is when the current groups start ('the week after next', in the first part), and that Saturday group is already 'full'.
❌ 3. In the spring: Spring is never mentioned; the only months she gives are January for the course and December for taking names.
✅ 4. In January: The woman says 'The next Saturday course starts in January.'

**Q4:** What is true about the woman?
- 1. She wants to check something with another teacher
- 2. She has added the man to the waiting list
- 3. She teaches the Tuesday evening group herself
- 4. She can sign him up for the January course today
- **Correct Answer:** Option 1
- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. She wants to check something with another teacher: She says 'Arjun teaches the Tuesday group, and he's in the back right now. Let me go and ask him something.'
❌ 2. She has added the man to the waiting list: She only tells him that 'four people are already on it'; she never puts his name down.
❌ 3. She teaches the Tuesday evening group herself: The full group is hers ('my Saturday group's full'), while 'Arjun teaches the Tuesday group.'
❌ 4. She can sign him up for the January course today: She will be 'taking names for that one in December', so she cannot sign him up for it today.

**Q5:** What is most likely true about the man?
- 1. He has a hockey game every Tuesday evening
- 2. He bought a new lens for the course yesterday
- 3. He would rather miss a class than a game
- 4. He is happy to wait for a later Saturday course
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. He has a hockey game every Tuesday evening: He corrects himself straight away: 'Well, every second Tuesday, anyway.'
❌ 2. He bought a new lens for the course yesterday: What he bought yesterday was 'a camera bag', not a lens.
✅ 3. He would rather miss a class than a game: He is 'the only goalie on my team', and when the woman says 'you'd be missing three of the six classes', he answers 'Yeah, I know' instead of offering to skip hockey.
❌ 4. He is happy to wait for a later Saturday course: He reacts with 'January?' and says 'I was hoping to get some decent heron shots before they fly south for the winter.'

**Q6:** What does the woman suggest?
- 1. Squeezing him into the Saturday morning group
- 2. Booking private lessons for the weeks he misses
- 3. Taking the Tuesday group and making up missed weeks
- 4. Coming to the Tuesday class after his games
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Squeezing him into the Saturday morning group: She never offers a place on Saturday mornings; the only Saturday time she mentions is the catch-up session 'on Saturday afternoons'.
❌ 2. Booking private lessons for the weeks he misses: This is the man's idea ('Could I just book private lessons on those weeks instead?'), and she points out that 'they're ninety dollars an hour.'
✅ 3. Taking the Tuesday group and making up missed weeks: She says 'on your hockey weeks, you could watch it online the next day', and Arjun runs 'a catch-up session' for 'anyone who missed that week'.
❌ 4. Coming to the Tuesday class after his games: She never suggests this; on his hockey weeks he would 'watch it online the next day' and go to the Saturday catch-up instead.

**Q7:** What does the woman agree to waive?
- 1. Part of the course fee
- 2. The cost of his course materials
- 3. The price of a private lesson
- 4. The fee for the catch-up sessions
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Part of the course fee: She says 'I can't change the course fee, that's up to the owner.'
✅ 2. The cost of his course materials: She says 'I can take off the forty-five-dollar materials fee. You'd still get the workbook.'
❌ 3. The price of a private lesson: Private lessons stay at 'ninety dollars an hour'; she offers no discount on them.
❌ 4. The fee for the catch-up sessions: There is no separate fee to waive, because 'The catch-up is included in the course.'

**Q8:** What will most likely happen next?
- 1. The man will join the Saturday waiting list
- 2. The man will fill in a registration form
- 3. The woman will ask the owner to lower the fee
- 4. The man will go home and read his camera manual
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The man will join the Saturday waiting list: He has just accepted the Tuesday plan ('you've talked me into it'), so he no longer needs a Saturday place.
✅ 2. The man will fill in a registration form: He agrees with 'you've talked me into it', and the woman says 'Let me grab you a form.'
❌ 3. The woman will ask the owner to lower the fee: The course fee is 'up to the owner', and she has already dealt with his worry about the price by taking off 'the forty-five-dollar materials fee'.
❌ 4. The man will go home and read his camera manual: She only asks him to 'bring your camera's manual to the first class'; right now she is getting him 'a form'.

## Exam 5 — Part 2: Park Sculpture Proposal

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between two neighbours. They are walking their dogs in a park in Kingston, Ontario, on a summer evening.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Evening, Nadia! Hot one, eh? Biscuit keeps pulling me toward the pond.
WOMAN: Hi, Omar. Pepper too. She'd jump in if I let her.
MAN: Hey, did you see the notice by the gate? The city wants to put a big sculpture here in Limestone Park.
WOMAN: Here? Seriously? What kind of sculpture?
MAN: A walk-through one. Tall, colourful steel arches you can walk under and touch. It's by the artist from Wolfe Island who did the turtle by the ferry dock.
WOMAN: Oh, I love that turtle. My nephew climbs all over it. But something that size can't be cheap. Who's paying for it?
MAN: Well, the city would put in part of it. The rest is supposed to come from private donations and an arts grant.
WOMAN: Supposed to. So they don't have it yet?
MAN: Not yet. They've applied, and they'll find out in the fall.
WOMAN: Hmm. My property tax went up again in January, and they still closed the outdoor pool early last summer. If that grant falls through, guess who covers the difference.
MAN: Fair point. Honestly, my worry's more the upkeep. Remember the splash pad by the playground? Broken for two whole summers.
WOMAN: Oh, don't remind me. The kids were so disappointed.
MAN: Right? But the notice says the parks department would handle repairs, and the flower bed volunteers have offered to clean the arches every couple of weeks.
WOMAN: The flower bed people? Oh, they'll do it. They're out here before us dog walkers every morning.
MAN: Anyway, they're asking for feedback. There's a table at the farmers' market this Saturday, and a public meeting next month.
WOMAN: Saturday's no good, I work. Where's the meeting?
MAN: The notice says city hall, but there's a sticker over it. They've moved it to the library on Bath Road.
WOMAN: Oh, good, that's a five-minute walk for me. City hall is two buses. When is it?
MAN: Thursday the twelfth, at seven.
WOMAN: Then I'm going. I want to hear what happens if that grant doesn't come through.
MAN: And I'll bring up the splash pad. Want to walk over together? I'll knock at twenty to seven.
WOMAN: Deal. But Pepper's staying home. She'd bark through the whole thing.
MAN: Biscuit too.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What has the man just found out?
- 1. The broken splash pad is finally going to be fixed.
- 2. Their park may get a large new work of art.
- 3. Volunteers are planting new flower beds by the gate.
- 4. The turtle statue is being moved to their park.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The broken splash pad is finally going to be fixed: The splash pad comes up only as the man's reason to worry about upkeep ("Broken for two whole summers"); the repairs on the notice are for the new arches, and nobody says the splash pad will be fixed.
✅ 2. Their park may get a large new work of art: The man says "The city wants to put a big sculpture here in Limestone Park," and the rest of the talk is about how it would be paid for, who would look after it and the meeting about it.
❌ 3. Volunteers are planting new flower beds by the gate: The notice is "by the gate," and the "flower bed volunteers have offered to clean" the sculpture; nobody mentions new flower beds.
❌ 4. The turtle statue is being moved to their park: The turtle is the artist's earlier work ("the artist from Wolfe Island who did the turtle by the ferry dock"), and nobody says it will move; the new piece is "Tall, colourful steel arches you can walk under and touch."

**Q2:** Who has offered to keep the sculpture clean?
- 1. Workers from the city's parks department
- 2. The artist from Wolfe Island
- 3. Volunteers who look after the flowers
- 4. Dog walkers who use the park
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Workers from the city's parks department: The notice says "the parks department would handle repairs," which is not the cleaning.
❌ 2. The artist from Wolfe Island: The artist is mentioned only as the maker of the arches and of "the turtle by the ferry dock"; nothing is said about the artist cleaning anything.
✅ 3. Volunteers who look after the flowers: The man says "the flower bed volunteers have offered to clean the arches every couple of weeks."
❌ 4. Dog walkers who use the park: The woman mentions dog walkers only to say the flower bed volunteers are out "before us dog walkers every morning"; the dog walkers have offered nothing.

**Q3:** Why is the man worried about the upkeep?
- 1. The city may not receive the arts grant.
- 2. Children could damage it by climbing all over it.
- 3. The outdoor pool was closed early last summer.
- 4. The splash pad stayed broken for a long time.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The city may not receive the arts grant: This is the woman's worry ("If that grant falls through, guess who covers the difference"), and it is about the cost, not the upkeep.
❌ 2. Children could damage it by climbing all over it: The woman says her nephew "climbs all over" the turtle by the ferry dock, but nobody says children could damage the new sculpture.
❌ 3. The outdoor pool was closed early last summer: The woman says this ("they still closed the outdoor pool early last summer") as part of her point about money; it is not the man's reason.
✅ 4. The splash pad stayed broken for a long time: The man says "my worry's more the upkeep. Remember the splash pad by the playground? Broken for two whole summers."

**Q4:** How does the woman seem to feel about the cost?
- 1. She suspects local taxpayers could end up paying more.
- 2. She is relieved that donations will cover most of it.
- 3. She feels it is worth the money for the children.
- 4. She is upset that it has raised her property tax.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 1
- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. She suspects local taxpayers could end up paying more: She points out that her "property tax went up again in January" and says "If that grant falls through, guess who covers the difference," meaning people like her; she also wants to hear "what happens if that grant doesn't come through."
❌ 2. She is relieved that donations will cover most of it: When the man says the rest is "supposed to come from private donations and an arts grant," she answers "Supposed to," which shows doubt, not relief.
❌ 3. She feels it is worth the money for the children: She loves the turtle and her nephew "climbs all over it," but about the new piece she says "something that size can't be cheap" and questions the funding.
❌ 4. She is upset that it has raised her property tax: Her tax went up "in January," and the sculpture is only a plan the city is "asking for feedback" on, so it has not raised her tax.

**Q5:** Where are the two of them planning to go together?
- 1. To an information table at the market
- 2. To a public meeting at city hall
- 3. To a public meeting at the library
- 4. To the ferry dock to see the turtle
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To an information table at the market: The feedback table at the farmers' market is "this Saturday," and the woman says "Saturday's no good, I work," so they will not go there together.
❌ 2. To a public meeting at city hall: The notice "says city hall, but there's a sticker over it. They've moved it to the library on Bath Road."
✅ 3. To a public meeting at the library: The meeting next month is now at "the library on Bath Road" on "Thursday the twelfth, at seven"; the man asks "Want to walk over together?" and the woman answers "Deal."
❌ 4. To the ferry dock to see the turtle: The turtle by the ferry dock comes up only as the artist's earlier work, and they make no plan to go there.

## Exam 5 — Part 3: Electronics Store Laptop Advice

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation. A woman is shopping for a laptop.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi there. You've been looking at these laptops for a while. Can I help?
WOMAN: Yes, please. It's not for me, though mine's practically an antique. My daughter, Hana, starts college in September, and she's never had her own laptop.
MAN: Good timing. Our back-to-school sale just started. What will she mostly use it for? Anything heavy, like video editing?
WOMAN: Oh, I didn't know about the sale. No editing, and gaming's her brother's department. Mostly essays, plus video calls with friends who are moving away. She watches her shows on her phone.
MAN: Then it's between these two. The fourteen-inch is just over a kilogram, with ten hours of battery, for $899. The fifteen-inch is $849, but almost two kilograms, with maybe six hours.
WOMAN: Fifty dollars is fifty dollars, though, and wouldn't the bigger screen be easier for writing? Mind you, she'll be on the bus every day, forty minutes each way.
MAN: Then think about that bus. An extra kilogram adds up fast every day, and the bigger screen only helps a little. For Hana, I'd go with the fourteen-inch.
WOMAN: That makes sense. Now, is there a student price?
MAN: Yes, seventy-five dollars off either one. But I'd have to scan her student card.
WOMAN: I've got her acceptance email on my phone. Would that do?
MAN: Sorry, emails and class schedules don't count, and neither do photos. It has to be the card itself.
WOMAN: Of course. She got it at orientation last week, but it's in her wallet at work. Could I pay today and bring the card in later?
MAN: Unfortunately, the discount can't be added afterwards. And you get fifteen days for returns, but an opened box costs a fifteen per cent restocking fee. So she should try the display model first.
WOMAN: Fair enough. Anything else?
MAN: Just our three-year protection plan, for $149. It covers drops and spills, which students are very good at.
WOMAN: Hmm. I bought one for my last phone, and when the screen cracked, suddenly that wasn't covered. I'll think about it, but don't hold your breath.
MAN: No pressure at all. The sale runs until Sunday, by the way.
WOMAN: Then here's the plan. Hana's off on Saturday, so I'll bring her in, card and all, to try both keyboards.
MAN: Sounds good. I'm working Saturday, so come find me.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** Why is the woman shopping for a laptop?
- 1. Her own laptop is getting too old.
- 2. Her daughter needs one for her studies.
- 3. Her son wants a computer for games.
- 4. The store is having a back-to-school sale.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Her own laptop is getting too old: She jokes that 'mine's practically an antique,' but she says the new laptop is 'not for me.'
✅ 2. Her daughter needs one for her studies: She says 'My daughter, Hana, starts college in September, and she's never had her own laptop.'
❌ 3. Her son wants a computer for games: The son comes up only because 'gaming's her brother's department'; the laptop is for her daughter.
❌ 4. The store is having a back-to-school sale: The man mentions the sale after she has explained why she is there, and she says 'I didn't know about the sale.'

**Q2:** What will the new laptop mostly be used for?
- 1. editing videos for her school projects
- 2. playing online games in her free time
- 3. writing papers and calling friends online
- 4. watching her favourite shows on a bigger screen
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. editing videos for her school projects: The man asks about 'video editing,' and she answers 'No editing.'
❌ 2. playing online games in her free time: She says 'gaming's her brother's department,' not her daughter's.
✅ 3. writing papers and calling friends online: She says 'Mostly essays, plus video calls with friends who are moving away.'
❌ 4. watching her favourite shows on a bigger screen: She says 'She watches her shows on her phone'; the bigger screen comes up only as a possible help 'for writing.'

**Q3:** Which laptop does the man recommend?
- 1. the 15-inch, because its bigger screen helps with writing
- 2. the 14-inch, because it is lighter for her daily trips
- 3. the 14-inch, because it costs less than the other one
- 4. the 15-inch, because it would save her fifty dollars
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. the 15-inch, because its bigger screen helps with writing: That is the woman's idea; the man says 'the bigger screen only helps a little' and recommends the fourteen-inch.
✅ 2. the 14-inch, because it is lighter for her daily trips: After she says she'll be 'on the bus every day,' he answers 'An extra kilogram adds up fast every day' and 'For Hana, I'd go with the fourteen-inch.'
❌ 3. the 14-inch, because it costs less than the other one: The fourteen-inch is the more expensive model at '$899,' while 'The fifteen-inch is $849.'
❌ 4. the 15-inch, because it would save her fifty dollars: The saving is the woman's point ('Fifty dollars is fifty dollars'); the man still recommends the fourteen-inch.

**Q4:** What is needed to get the student price?
- 1. the acceptance email from her college
- 2. a printed copy of her class schedule
- 3. the actual card she got at orientation
- 4. a clear photo of her student card
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. the acceptance email from her college: The woman offers it, but the man says 'emails and class schedules don't count.'
❌ 2. a printed copy of her class schedule: The man says 'emails and class schedules don't count.'
✅ 3. the actual card she got at orientation: He says 'It has to be the card itself,' and the woman explains 'She got it at orientation last week.'
❌ 4. a clear photo of her student card: Photos are ruled out too; the man says 'neither do photos.'

**Q5:** How does the woman react to the protection plan?
- 1. She is keen on it, since students often spill things.
- 2. She is doubtful, since a past plan let her down.
- 3. She is confused, since its coverage was not explained.
- 4. She is annoyed, since the man keeps pushing it.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She is keen on it, since students often spill things: The remark that students are 'very good at' drops and spills is the man's joke, and she answers 'don't hold your breath.'
✅ 2. She is doubtful, since a past plan let her down: She recalls that on her last phone, 'when the screen cracked, suddenly that wasn't covered,' then adds 'I'll think about it, but don't hold your breath.'
❌ 3. She is confused, since its coverage was not explained: The man states plainly that 'It covers drops and spills,' and she asks nothing more about it.
❌ 4. She is annoyed, since the man keeps pushing it: He mentions the plan only once and then says 'No pressure at all.'

**Q6:** What is the woman's plan for Saturday?
- 1. to come back to the store with her daughter
- 2. to buy the laptop and bring the card in later
- 3. to pick up her daughter's card at the college
- 4. to get the card from her daughter's workplace
- **Correct Answer:** Option 1
- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. to come back to the store with her daughter: She says 'Hana's off on Saturday, so I'll bring her in, card and all, to try both keyboards.'
❌ 2. to buy the laptop and bring the card in later: She asks about paying today, but the man says 'the discount can't be added afterwards.'
❌ 3. to pick up her daughter's card at the college: Hana already has the card; 'She got it at orientation last week.'
❌ 4. to get the card from her daughter's workplace: The card is 'in her wallet at work' today, but Hana is 'off on Saturday' and is coming in with it.

## Exam 5 — Part 4: Hearing Implant Switch-On

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a news item about a man who had his hearing restored.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** With the implant, the first voice MacLellan understood clearly was .....
- 1. his wife's, the moment it was turned on.
- 2. his granddaughter's, once it was adjusted.
- 3. the audiologist's, as she first tested it.
- 4. his surgeon's, the day after his operation.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. his wife's, the moment it was turned on: When the implant was turned on, "every voice, even his wife Flora's, sounded like a robot in a tin can, and he couldn't make out a word."
✅ 2. his granddaughter's, once it was adjusted: "After some adjustments, his granddaughter Ellie leaned in and asked if he could hear her," and he said, "This time, I understood every word."
❌ 3. the audiologist's, as she first tested it: When the implant was first turned on, "every voice" sounded "like a robot in a tin can, and he couldn't make out a word"; the first voice he understood came only "after some adjustments," and it was Ellie's.
❌ 4. his surgeon's, the day after his operation: The implant was not working then, because "Doctors kept the implant switched off for a month after his operation, while he healed."

**Q2:** MacLellan's hearing loss was mainly caused by .....
- 1. the normal effects of growing older.
- 2. years of loud music with his fiddle group.
- 3. decades of noise from his boat's motor.
- 4. the constant wind and waves at sea.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. the normal effects of growing older: Age was only part of the cause, since "Doctors say age played a part, but the engine did most of the damage."
❌ 2. years of loud music with his fiddle group: The fiddle group is where his hearing loss showed ("he couldn't hear the other players"), not what caused it; the damage came from "a roaring diesel engine."
✅ 3. decades of noise from his boat's motor: He "fished out of Neils Harbour, Nova Scotia, for forty years beside a roaring diesel engine, without ear protection," and "the engine did most of the damage."
❌ 4. the constant wind and waves at sea: Wind and waves are never mentioned; the cause given is the "roaring diesel engine," which "did most of the damage."

**Q3:** Being able to understand a voice again left MacLellan .....
- 1. annoyed that voices still sounded like robots.
- 2. too overcome with emotion to reply.
- 3. laughing at how strange everyone sounded.
- 4. proud he had gone ahead with the operation.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. annoyed that voices still sounded like robots: The robot sound came before the adjustments, and once he understood Ellie he showed no annoyance: "I just sat there crying."
✅ 2. too overcome with emotion to reply: "I wanted to answer her, but nothing came out. I just sat there crying."
❌ 3. laughing at how strange everyone sounded: Voices did sound "like a robot in a tin can" at first, but he was not laughing: "I just sat there crying."
❌ 4. proud he had gone ahead with the operation: He says nothing about pride or about the operation, which happened a month earlier; when he understood Ellie, "nothing came out. I just sat there crying."

**Q4:** So far, the implant has allowed MacLellan to .....
- 1. talk easily with his family on the phone.
- 2. hear voices that no longer sound tinny.
- 3. keep up with conversations at mealtimes.
- 4. play with his old fiddle group again.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. talk easily with his family on the phone: The phone is still a problem, since "phone calls are hard."
❌ 2. hear voices that no longer sound tinny: The tinny sound has not gone away: "Voices still sound tinny."
✅ 3. keep up with conversations at mealtimes: "MacLellan can follow the talk at the supper table again."
❌ 4. play with his old fiddle group again: That has not happened yet; it is only his goal: "He hopes to rejoin the fiddle group by spring."

**Q5:** The audiologist told MacLellan to .....
- 1. keep the implant off until he had healed.
- 2. set aside some listening time each day.
- 3. wait until spring to play his fiddle again.
- 4. stay away from loud engines from now on.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. keep the implant off until he had healed: That happened before the switch-on and was the doctors' decision: "Doctors kept the implant switched off for a month after his operation, while he healed."
✅ 2. set aside some listening time each day: Nisha Varma told him, "Listen to something every single day: the radio, an audiobook, your family."
❌ 3. wait until spring to play his fiddle again: Spring is MacLellan's own goal ("He hopes to rejoin the fiddle group by spring"), not the audiologist's advice.
❌ 4. stay away from loud engines from now on: The engine caused his hearing loss, but the audiologist's advice was about practice: "Listen to something every single day."

## Exam 5 — Part 5: VR Tournament Format

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a discussion among three members of a local gaming club. They are getting ready for the club's first virtual reality tournament.

### Audio Transcript
A: Okay, guys, Glenview Community Hall is booked for Saturday the twenty-first, noon to six. Now we figure out how our first VR tournament actually runs.
B: How many players are we looking at, Mateo?
A: Forty so far, and registration's open till Friday, so I'm expecting around fifty.
B: Fifty? Our spring game night only got thirty!
C: Great, but the hall isn't exactly huge. It's rated for sixty, and every headset needs two metres of clear floor.
A: That's why we're streaming it, so families can watch from home. Now, format. Hamza, you wanted round-robin?
B: Everyone plays everyone. Players are paying fifteen bucks to get in. Nobody wants to come across town, lose one match and go home.
C: With fifty people? That'd take till next Tuesday. Ten headsets, six hours. Straight elimination's the only thing that fits.
B: And half the room's knocked out by one o'clock. That's not a tournament, that's a waiting room.
A: He's got a point, Connor. So do you. What if we split it? Groups of five, four matches each, then the top two in each group play elimination finals.
B: Look at him, he's had that up his sleeve all week. I could live with that.
C: I'm in, as long as every match has a hard ten-minute limit. One slow puzzle round wrecks the schedule.
A: Fair. We keep our three categories, action, puzzle and sports.
B: Same prizes too? Gaming gear for the top three, something smaller for each category winner, a club T-shirt for everyone.
C: Who's running the stream?
B: My cousin and his friends. They stream every weekend, and they'd do it for pizza.
C: The same guys who ran the sound at our holiday party?
B: Okay, that was one time.
A: Hamza, look at Connor. He's been watching the clock the whole time.
C: Because the caretaker locks up at six sharp. If we're still packing up, it's a hundred dollars every half hour, on my credit card.
A: Which is why we test it first. The Saturday before, club members only, same format, same timer.
B: Good. If something breaks, better now than on the day.
C: Fine by me. But if the test runs long, we cut the groups to four.
B: Whoa, one thing at a time. Let's see how the test goes.
A: Agreed. I'll send the invite to club members tonight.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the discussion mainly about?
- 1. where the club should hold its first VR tournament
- 2. how the club should organize its first VR tournament
- 3. who will stream the tournament for viewers at home
- 4. which prizes the tournament's top players should get
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. where the club should hold its first VR tournament: That is already settled. Mateo opens with "Glenview Community Hall is booked for Saturday the twenty-first, noon to six."
✅ 2. how the club should organize its first VR tournament: Mateo sets the task at the start ("Now we figure out how our first VR tournament actually runs"), and most of the talk is about the match format, a time limit for each match and a test run.
❌ 3. who will stream the tournament for viewers at home: The stream comes up only briefly. Connor asks "Who's running the stream?" and Hamza's cousin and his friends take it on in one line.
❌ 4. which prizes the tournament's top players should get: The prizes are only confirmed, not debated. Hamza checks that they stay the same ("Same prizes too?") and nobody changes them.

**Q2:** What turnout is Mateo expecting?
- 1. about thirty players
- 2. about forty players
- 3. about fifty players
- 4. about sixty players
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. about thirty players: Thirty is how many people came to an earlier event. Hamza says "Our spring game night only got thirty!"
❌ 2. about forty players: Forty is only how many have signed up "so far." Mateo adds that "registration's open till Friday," so he expects more.
✅ 3. about fifty players: Mateo says "Forty so far, and registration's open till Friday, so I'm expecting around fifty."
❌ 4. about sixty players: Sixty is the hall's limit, not a number of players. Connor says "It's rated for sixty."

**Q3:** What is Connor pointing out when he says the hall 'isn't exactly huge'?
- 1. it is a good size for a first tournament
- 2. it is too far across town for some players
- 3. it could get crowded once everyone is inside
- 4. it can only be booked for six hours
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. it is a good size for a first tournament: Connor's "Great, but" welcomes the number of players, not the hall. He goes on to warn that it is "rated for sixty" and that "every headset needs two metres of clear floor."
❌ 2. it is too far across town for some players: Hamza's "across town" comes later ("Nobody wants to come across town"), and it is about travelling to play only one match. Connor's remark is about the size of the room.
✅ 3. it could get crowded once everyone is inside: Saying the hall "isn't exactly huge" is a polite way of saying it is small. With about fifty players, Connor points out it is "rated for sixty" and "every headset needs two metres of clear floor," and Mateo answers by streaming the event "so families can watch from home."
❌ 4. it can only be booked for six hours: The hall is booked "noon to six," but that is a limit on time. Connor's remark is about how much space there is.

**Q4:** Why does Hamza prefer a round-robin?
- 1. he thinks a full round-robin could still fit in six hours
- 2. he feels paying players should get more than one match
- 3. he says most players are travelling from out of town
- 4. he thinks the spring game night showed players like long events
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. he thinks a full round-robin could still fit in six hours: Hamza never says this. Connor answers "That'd take till next Tuesday," and Hamza replies by attacking straight elimination, not by defending the timing.
✅ 2. he feels paying players should get more than one match: Hamza says "Players are paying fifteen bucks to get in. Nobody wants to come across town, lose one match and go home."
❌ 3. he says most players are travelling from out of town: Hamza only says players come "across town," which means from another part of the same city, and his point is that nobody wants to "lose one match and go home."
❌ 4. he thinks the spring game night showed players like long events: Hamza mentions the spring game night only to compare numbers ("only got thirty"). He says nothing about how long it lasted.

**Q5:** How does Connor respond to Mateo's plan for groups?
- 1. he still thinks only straight elimination will fit the day
- 2. he now thinks a full round-robin would be fairer
- 3. he agrees, but only if each match is strictly timed
- 4. he wants the puzzle games left out of the group rounds
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. he still thinks only straight elimination will fit the day: That was his first position ("Straight elimination's the only thing that fits"), but when Mateo suggests groups he says "I'm in."
❌ 2. he now thinks a full round-robin would be fairer: The full round-robin is Hamza's idea. Connor's view of it is "With fifty people? That'd take till next Tuesday," and he never changes his mind.
✅ 3. he agrees, but only if each match is strictly timed: Connor says "I'm in, as long as every match has a hard ten-minute limit."
❌ 4. he wants the puzzle games left out of the group rounds: Connor mentions "One slow puzzle round" only to show why a time limit matters. He never asks to drop puzzle games, and Mateo then confirms "action, puzzle and sports."

**Q6:** What does Hamza's reply about the holiday party suggest?
- 1. his cousin's friends will want more than pizza
- 2. his cousin's group had trouble running the sound
- 3. his cousin has never run a live stream before
- 4. he will find someone else to run the stream
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. his cousin's friends will want more than pizza: Hamza says the opposite when he adds that "they'd do it for pizza."
✅ 2. his cousin's group had trouble running the sound: Connor asks "The same guys who ran the sound at our holiday party?" and Hamza answers "Okay, that was one time." He admits that something went wrong at the party, while insisting it happened only once.
❌ 3. his cousin has never run a live stream before: Hamza says his cousin and his friends "stream every weekend," so they have plenty of experience.
❌ 4. he will find someone else to run the stream: Hamza's "Okay" admits the problem but does not drop his cousin's group. He defends them with "that was one time," and nobody suggests another crew before Mateo changes the subject ("Hamza, look at Connor").

**Q7:** How will Connor be affected if the club is still in the hall after six?
- 1. he will have to lock up the hall himself
- 2. he will have to give players their entry fees back
- 3. he will have to pay extra on his credit card
- 4. he will have to pack up all ten headsets alone
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. he will have to lock up the hall himself: Locking up is the caretaker's job. Connor says "the caretaker locks up at six sharp."
❌ 2. he will have to give players their entry fees back: The "fifteen bucks" entry fee comes up only in Hamza's case for a round-robin. Nobody mentions refunds.
✅ 3. he will have to pay extra on his credit card: Connor says that if they are "still packing up," "it's a hundred dollars every half hour, on my credit card."
❌ 4. he will have to pack up all ten headsets alone: Connor mentions "packing up" only as the reason they might run late. Nobody says he will do it alone.

**Q8:** Which next step do Mateo, Hamza and Connor all accept?
- 1. cutting the groups to four players to save time
- 2. asking the caretaker to let them stay past six
- 3. trying out the format with club members first
- 4. inviting every registered player to a practice day
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. cutting the groups to four players to save time: Only Connor wants this, and only if the test runs long ("we cut the groups to four"). Hamza pushes back ("Whoa, one thing at a time"), and Mateo agrees with Hamza.
❌ 2. asking the caretaker to let them stay past six: Nobody suggests asking the caretaker for more time. Connor says "the caretaker locks up at six sharp," which is why timing matters.
✅ 3. trying out the format with club members first: Mateo says "we test it first. The Saturday before, club members only, same format, same timer." Hamza says "Good" and Connor says "Fine by me."
❌ 4. inviting every registered player to a practice day: The test is for "club members only," and Mateo will send the invite "to club members tonight," not to everyone who has registered.

## Exam 5 — Part 6: AI Tools in Schoolwork

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a speech about students using AI tools for schoolwork.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** Marc Gagnon is speaking .....
- 1. to parents who will vote on the rule next month
- 2. to parents at an evening about their children's courses
- 3. at a staff meeting where a student shared a story
- 4. to students who answered the English department's survey
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. to parents who will vote on the rule next month: His listeners are parents, but the vote belongs to the staff ("a rule our staff will vote on next month"); he only asks parents for their views "before the vote."
✅ 2. to parents at an evening about their children's courses: He opens with "Thanks for coming out to curriculum night" and talks to people about to "meet your kids' teachers," which makes them parents.
❌ 3. at a staff meeting where a student shared a story: Aaliyah Grant told her story earlier, at "our last staff meeting"; tonight's event is "curriculum night."
❌ 4. to students who answered the English department's survey: The survey went to "our grade ten and eleven students" last spring; his listeners tonight are people whose kids attend the school.

**Q2:** Hélène Tremblay believes that .....
- 1. students should be free to use the tools without saying so
- 2. more essays should be written in class on paper
- 3. open use of the tools is better than hidden use
- 4. most students already tell teachers when they use the tools
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. students should be free to use the tools without saying so: She accepts that "They're using it either way," but under her rule students "would add a short note to each assignment saying what the tool did."
❌ 2. more essays should be written in class on paper: This is Peter Kaminski's idea; "he'd like more essays written in class, on paper."
✅ 3. open use of the tools is better than hidden use: After her survey found that most students "had never told a teacher," she says, "I'd rather it happened where we can see it."
❌ 4. most students already tell teachers when they use the tools: Her survey found the opposite; "most had never told a teacher."

**Q3:** Peter Kaminski opposes the rule because he thinks .....
- 1. students will keep their use of the tools hidden
- 2. a chatbot could do students' thinking for them
- 3. students in his class had copied from one another
- 4. the notes would mean extra work for teachers
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. students will keep their use of the tools hidden: Hidden use is what Hélène Tremblay's survey found ("most had never told a teacher"); Kaminski's class used a chatbot with his permission ("he let one of his grade ten classes use a chatbot"), so hiding it is not his point.
✅ 2. a chatbot could do students' thinking for them: He says "Working out what you think is the whole point of an essay" and "If a machine hands you the arguments, you've skipped the part where you learn something."
❌ 3. students in his class had copied from one another: The eleven essays with "the same three arguments, in the same order" came from a class that used "a chatbot to plan an essay"; his complaint is about what a machine hands students, and nobody is said to have copied.
❌ 4. the notes would mean extra work for teachers: He never mentions extra work; he simply prefers essays "written in class, on paper" to "notes on every assignment."

**Q4:** If the staff vote for the rule, it will first be tried .....
- 1. in every class at the school for a full year
- 2. in grade 10 history classes from October on
- 3. in a single English course for one term
- 4. in grade 10 and 11 English classes for a term
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. in every class at the school for a full year: The school would "look at the results before deciding about the rest of the school," so the rule would not start everywhere at once.
❌ 2. in grade 10 history classes from October on: A grade ten history class is where Kaminski tried a chatbot "Last year," and October ninth is the date of the staff vote, not of the trial.
✅ 3. in a single English course for one term: "If the rule passes, we'd try it for one term, in grade eleven English only."
❌ 4. in grade 10 and 11 English classes for a term: Grades ten and eleven are the students in last spring's survey; the trial is "in grade eleven English only," so grade 10 English is left out."

**Q5:** Aaliyah Grant's story about her two classes implies that .....
- 1. her chemistry teacher had gone against a school rule
- 2. her teachers have different ideas about what's allowed
- 3. she lost marks in French for not declaring her chatbot use
- 4. chatbots often make mistakes when they check students' work
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. her chemistry teacher had gone against a school rule: There is no school rule to break yet; the proposed rule "would also be our first school-wide rule on these tools."
✅ 2. her teachers have different ideas about what's allowed: Her chemistry teacher "showed us how to have a chatbot check our lab reports," but "The same week, I lost marks in French for doing exactly that," so one teacher welcomes what another punishes.
❌ 3. she lost marks in French for not declaring her chatbot use: She lost marks "for doing exactly that," that is, for having a chatbot check her work; declaring use is part of the rule that is only being proposed.
❌ 4. chatbots often make mistakes when they check students' work: She never says the chatbot got anything wrong; the marks came off for the use itself, "for doing exactly that."

**Q6:** Hélène Tremblay and Peter Kaminski disagree about the rule, but both .....
- 1. want students to add a note to each assignment
- 2. have tried a chatbot with one of their own classes
- 3. accept that the tools give feedback very quickly
- 4. doubt that the feedback from chatbots is any good
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. want students to add a note to each assignment: Only Tremblay wants this ("students would add a short note to each assignment"); Kaminski would have essays written in class "Instead of notes on every assignment."
❌ 2. have tried a chatbot with one of their own classes: Only Kaminski did this ("he let one of his grade ten classes use a chatbot"); nothing is said about Tremblay trying one with a class.
✅ 3. accept that the tools give feedback very quickly: Tremblay likes that a stuck student "can get useful feedback within seconds," and Kaminski "admits the feedback came fast."
❌ 4. doubt that the feedback from chatbots is any good: Neither does; Tremblay calls the feedback "useful," and Kaminski admits "some of it was good." They agree on its speed, not on doubting its quality."

## Exam 50 — Part 1: Fitness Trial Enrolment

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman at a community fitness center. The woman works at the fitness center, and the man is a new customer.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Excuse me, I'm interested in joining this fitness center. Could you tell me about the different membership options you have?
WOMAN: Of course! We have several plans to choose from. Our basic membership gives you access to all the equipment and facilities for $45 per month. The premium plan at $65 includes unlimited fitness classes as well.
MAN: Hmm, I'm not sure which would be better for me. I've never really been to a gym before, to be honest.
WOMAN: Well, if you're just starting out, we actually have a two-week trial membership for $25. That way you can try everything and see what works for you before committing to a full membership.
MAN: That sounds perfect. Do I need to sign up for that today?
WOMAN: You can, or you can think about it. The trial offer isn't going anywhere. But I should mention that if you do sign up today, we're waiving the usual $15 registration fee as part of our summer promotion.
MAN: Oh, that's good to know. I think I'll go ahead with the trial then. What do I need to do?

WOMAN: Great choice! I just need you to fill out this form with your contact information, and then I'll need to see a piece of photo ID.
MAN: Sure, here's my driver's license. Um, I was wondering—does the trial membership include an orientation session? I'm a bit nervous about using some of the equipment incorrectly.
WOMAN: Absolutely! We actually require all new members to have a brief orientation. We can schedule that right now if you'd like.
MAN: That would be great. I'm free most evenings after 6.
WOMAN: Let me check our schedule... We have an opening tomorrow at 6:30 with Mike, one of our personal trainers. Would that work for you?
MAN: Tomorrow at 6:30 sounds perfect. How long does the orientation usually take?
WOMAN: It's about 45 minutes. Mike will show you how to use the equipment safely and help you set some initial fitness goals based on what you're hoping to achieve.
MAN: That's exactly what I need. And what should I bring with me tomorrow?

WOMAN: Just bring comfortable workout clothes, a water bottle, and a small towel if you have one. We do have towels available for rent at $2, but many members prefer to bring their own.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the cost of the trial membership?
- 1. $$15
- 2. $$25
- 3. $$45
- 4. $$65
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. $15: This is the registration fee that's being waived, not the trial membership cost.
✅ 2. $25: The woman clearly states "we actually have a two-week trial membership for $25."
❌ 3. $45: This is the cost of the basic monthly membership, not the trial.
❌ 4. $65: This is the cost of the premium monthly membership, not the trial.

**Q2:** What special offer is available today?
- 1. A discounted monthly rate
- 2. A free personal training session
- 3. No registration fee
- 4. Extended trial period
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. A discounted monthly rate: No discounted monthly rate is mentioned.
❌ 2. A free personal training session: The orientation is required for all members, not a special offer.
✅ 3. No registration fee: The woman specifically mentions "if you do sign up today, we're waiving the usual $15 registration fee as part of our summer promotion."
❌ 4. Extended trial period: No extension of the trial period is mentioned.

**Q3:** What is true about the man?
- 1. He has been a member before
- 2. He is experienced with gym equipment
- 3. He is concerned about using equipment properly
- 4. He wants to take fitness classes immediately
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. He has been a member before: He explicitly states "I've never really been to a gym before."
❌ 2. He is experienced with gym equipment: He expresses nervousness about using equipment incorrectly, indicating inexperience.
✅ 3. He is concerned about using equipment properly: He directly states "I'm a bit nervous about using some of the equipment incorrectly" and asks about orientation.
❌ 4. He wants to take fitness classes immediately: He doesn't express any specific interest in fitness classes.

**Q4:** When is the man's orientation scheduled?
- 1. Today at 6:00 PM
- 2. Tomorrow at 6:30 PM
- 3. This weekend at 8:00 AM
- 4. Next week at 4:00 PM
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Today at 6:00 PM: The orientation is not scheduled for today.
✅ 2. Tomorrow at 6:30 PM: The woman specifically says "We have an opening tomorrow at 6:30 with Mike" and the man confirms this time works for him.
❌ 3. This weekend at 8:00 AM: No weekend appointment is mentioned.
❌ 4. Next week at 4:00 PM: No appointment for next week is discussed.

**Q5:** How long will the orientation session last?
- 1. 30 minutes
- 2. 45 minutes
- 3. 60 minutes
- 4. 90 minutes
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2

## Exam 50 — Part 3: Dog Walking Rates

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a woman and a man about a dog walking service.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN:	Hi there, I noticed your flyer about dog walking services at the community center. I've just adopted a golden retriever and I work full-time, so I'm looking for someone reliable to walk him during weekdays.
MAN:	Thanks for calling! Congratulations on your new pet. I'd be happy to help you out. I've been running my dog walking service for about three years now, and I currently walk dogs in your neighborhood Monday through Friday.
WOMAN:	That sounds perfect. My dog, Buddy, is very energetic and needs a good walk at least once a day. What are your rates, and how long are the typical walks?
MAN:	I offer 30-minute walks for $18 and 60-minute walks for $28. Most of my clients choose the hour-long option for high-energy breeds like retrievers. I also offer a weekly package of five 60-minute walks for $125, which saves you $15 per week.
WOMAN:	The weekly package sounds like a good deal. What time would you be able to come by? I leave for work at 8:30 in the morning and don't get back until around 5:30.
MAN:	I could fit Buddy in around 12:30 pm each day. Would that work for you? I try to keep a consistent schedule so the dogs know when to expect their walks.
WOMAN:	That timing would be perfect. Do you take the dogs to any particular places? There's a nice park about two blocks from my house that Buddy really enjoys.
MAN:	Absolutely! I'm familiar with that park. It has a fenced area where dogs can run off-leash, right? I typically take the dogs to nearby parks or on neighborhood routes, depending on the owner's preference and the dog's needs.
WOMAN:	Yes, that's the one. Buddy loves it there. One more question - what happens if the weather is really bad? We get some heavy rainstorms this time of year.
MAN:	Great question. For light rain, we still go out with rain gear. For severe weather like thunderstorms or extreme temperatures, I offer a shorter 15-minute walk just for a bathroom break, and then some indoor playtime to burn off energy. There's no additional charge for this alternative.
WOMAN:	That sounds reasonable. When would you be able to start? And do you need to meet Buddy first?
MAN:	I always recommend a meet-and-greet session before starting regular service. It helps the dog get comfortable with me, and I can learn about any special needs or commands. I'm available this Saturday morning if that works for you.
WOMAN:	Saturday morning would be perfect. Let's say around 10:00? I'll text you my address if you give me your number. And if all goes well, perhaps you could start the regular walks next Monday?
MAN:	That sounds great. I'll put you in my calendar for Saturday at 10:00, and we can plan to start the regular schedule on Monday. I'm looking forward to meeting Buddy!
